### Welcome to Postman! This is your first collection. 

Collections are your starting point for building and testing APIs. You can use this one to:

• Group related requests
• Test your API in real-world scenarios
• Document and share your requests

Update the name and overview whenever you’re ready to make it yours.

[Learn more about Postman Collections.](https://learning.postman.com/docs/collections/collections-overview/)

request.description:
## Health Check

Checks whether the API server is up and running.

**Endpoint:** `GET /health`  
**Base URL:** `http://localhost:5000`

### Request

No request body or query parameters are required.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Method | GET |
| URL | `http://localhost:5000/health` |
| Auth | None |
| Body | None |

### Response

A successful response returns HTTP **200 OK**, indicating the server is healthy and accepting requests.

**Response fields:**

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | string | Server status, always `"ok"` when healthy |
| `timestamp` | string | ISO 8601 date-time of when the request was handled |
| `uptime` | string | How long the server has been running (in seconds) |

### Test

This request includes an automated test that verifies the response status code is `200`.

Returns metadata about the API, including its name, version, runtime environment, Node.js version, and a list of all available endpoints with their HTTP methods, paths, and descriptions.

## Request

**Method:** GET  
**URL:** `http://localhost:5000/api/info`

No request parameters, headers, or body are required.

## Response

**Status:** `200 OK`  
**Content-Type:** `application/json`

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | The name of the API project |
| `version` | string | The current version of the API |
| `environment` | string | The runtime environment (e.g. `development`, `production`) |
| `node` | string | The Node.js version the server is running on |
| `endpoints` | array | List of available API endpoints |
| `endpoints[].method` | string | HTTP method for the endpoint |
| `endpoints[].path` | string | URL path for the endpoint |
| `endpoints[].description` | string | Short description of what the endpoint does |

## Example Response

```json
{
  "name": "basic-rest-api",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "environment": "development",
  "node": "v22.18.0",
  "endpoints": [
    { "method": "GET", "path": "/health", "description": "Health check" },
    { "method": "GET", "path": "/api/info", "description": "API information" },
    { "method": "GET", "path": "/api/echo/:msg", "description": "Echo a message" }
  ]
}
```

## Echo Message

Returns the message provided in the URL path parameter, optionally converted to uppercase.

**Endpoint:** `GET /api/echo/:msg`
**Base URL:** `http://localhost:5000`

---

## Request

### URL Parameter

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `msg` | string | Yes | The message to echo back. Cannot be empty. |

### Query Parameter

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `upper` | boolean | No | If set to `true`, the echoed message is returned in uppercase. Defaults to `false`. |

### Example URLs

- `GET http://localhost:5000/api/echo/hello` — echoes `"hello"`
- `GET http://localhost:5000/api/echo/hello?upper=true` — echoes `"HELLO"`

---

## Response

### Success — `200 OK`

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `original` | string | The original message as provided in the URL parameter |
| `echoed` | string | The echoed message (uppercased if `upper=true`) |
| `upper` | boolean | Whether uppercase conversion was applied |
| `timestamp` | string | ISO 8601 date-time of when the request was handled |

**Example:**
```json
{
  "original": "hello",
  "echoed": "HELLO",
  "upper": true,
  "timestamp": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
}
```

### Error — `400 Bad Request`

Returned when the `:msg` parameter is empty.

```json
{
  "error": "Bad Request",
  "message": "Parameter :msg tidak boleh kosong."
}
```

Echoes back a message provided as a URL path parameter, with optional uppercase transformation.

**Endpoint:** `GET /api/echo/:msg`

## Path Parameters

| Name | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `msg` | Yes | The message to echo back. Must not be empty or blank. |

## Query Parameters

| Name | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `upper` | No | Set to `true` to return the echoed message in uppercase. Any other value (or omitting it) returns the message as-is. |

## Response

**200 OK**

``` json
{
  "original": "HelloWorld",
  "echoed": "HELLOWORLD",
  "upper": true,
  "timestamp": "2026-06-04T08:57:58.750Z"
}

 ```

**400 Bad Request** — when `:msg` is empty or whitespace:

``` json
{
  "error": "Bad Request",
  "message": "Parameter :msg tidak boleh kosong."
}

 ```

Tests the API's handling of requests to undefined or non-existent routes. Sending a GET request to a route that does not exist (e.g. `/api/tidakada`) should return a `404 Not Found` response with a JSON error body containing:

- `error.code`: `"NOT_FOUND"`
    
- `error.message`: a human-readable message indicating the route was not found
    
- `error.hint`: a suggestion to visit `GET /api/docs` for API documentation
    

Use this request to verify that the global 404 handler is working correctly.

Retrieves a list of all tasks.

**Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/tasks`

**Query Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `status` | string | No | Filter tasks by status. Accepted values: `todo`, `in_progress`, `done` |
| `priority` | string | No | Filter tasks by priority. Accepted values: `low`, `medium`, `high` |
| `limit` | integer | No | Maximum number of tasks to return per page |
| `offset` | integer | No | Number of tasks to skip (for pagination) |
| `sort` | string | No | Field to sort by (e.g. `createdAt`) |
| `order` | string | No | Sort direction. Accepted values: `asc`, `desc` |

**Response**

Returns a JSON object with a `data` array of task objects and a `pagination` object.

Each task object contains:
- `id` — Unique task identifier
- `title` — Task title
- `status` — Current status (`todo`, `in_progress`, `done`)
- `priority` — Priority level (`low`, `medium`, `high`)
- `createdAt` — ISO 8601 timestamp of creation
- `updatedAt` — ISO 8601 timestamp of last update

The `pagination` object contains:
- `total` — Total number of tasks matching the query
- `limit` — Applied limit
- `offset` — Applied offset
- `hasNext` — Whether a next page exists
- `hasPrev` — Whether a previous page exists
- `nextOffset` — Offset value for the next page
- `prevOffset` — Offset value for the previous page

**Example Response**
```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 5,
      "title": "Belajar GraphQL",
      "status": "todo",
      "priority": "low",
      "createdAt": "2024-01-14T00:00:00.000Z",
      "updatedAt": "2024-01-14T00:00:00.000Z"
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "total": 5,
    "limit": null,
    "offset": null,
    "hasNext": false,
    "hasPrev": false,
    "nextOffset": null,
    "prevOffset": null
  }
}
```

## Get All Tasks — Filtered by Status: `todo`

Retrieves a list of all tasks that have a status of **`todo`**. This endpoint is useful for fetching only the pending/unstarted tasks from the task list.

---

## HTTP Method & URL

```
GET http://localhost:5000/api/v1/tasks?status=todo
```

---

## Query Parameters

| Name | Type | Description | Example |
|------|------|-------------|---------|
| `status` | `string` | Filters tasks by their current status. Use `todo` to retrieve only tasks that have not been started yet. | `todo` |

---

## Sample Successful Response

**Status Code:** `200 OK`

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 5,
      "title": "Belajar GraphQL",
      "status": "todo",
      "priority": "low",
      "createdAt": "2024-01-14T00:00:00.000Z",
      "updatedAt": "2024-01-14T00:00:00.000Z"
    },
    {
      "id": 4,
      "title": "Setup PostgreSQL",
      "status": "todo",
      "priority": "medium",
      "createdAt": "2024-01-13T00:00:00.000Z",
      "updatedAt": "2024-01-13T00:00:00.000Z"
    },
    {
      "id": 3,
      "title": "Desain REST API",
      "status": "todo",
      "priority": "medium",
      "createdAt": "2024-01-12T00:00:00.000Z",
      "updatedAt": "2024-01-12T00:00:00.000Z"
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "total": 3,
    "limit": null,
    "offset": null,
    "hasNext": false,
    "hasPrev": false,
    "nextOffset": null,
    "prevOffset": null
  }
}
```

### Response Fields

**`data[]` — Array of task objects**

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `id` | `integer` | Unique identifier for the task. |
| `title` | `string` | The title or name of the task. |
| `status` | `string` | Current status of the task. Will always be `"todo"` for this filtered request. |
| `priority` | `string` | Priority level of the task. Possible values: `low`, `medium`, `high`. |
| `createdAt` | `string (ISO 8601)` | Timestamp indicating when the task was created. |
| `updatedAt` | `string (ISO 8601)` | Timestamp indicating when the task was last updated. |

**`pagination` — Pagination metadata**

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `total` | `integer` | Total number of tasks matching the filter. |
| `limit` | `integer \| null` | Maximum number of tasks returned per page. `null` if no limit is applied. |
| `offset` | `integer \| null` | Number of tasks skipped. `null` if no offset is applied. |
| `hasNext` | `boolean` | Indicates whether there is a next page of results. |
| `hasPrev` | `boolean` | Indicates whether there is a previous page of results. |
| `nextOffset` | `integer \| null` | Offset value to use for fetching the next page. `null` if no next page exists. |
| `prevOffset` | `integer \| null` | Offset value to use for fetching the previous page. `null` if no previous page exists. |
